rules.label: Colorado Hospital Discounted Care (HDC)
rules.quote: Patients who are at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines (FPG) are eligible for Hospital Discounted Care

rules.label: Denver Health Sliding Fee Discount Program (DHSFDP) for non-emergency care
rules.quote: You MUST live in Denver County to receive non-emergent care at Denver Health under the DHSFDP

rules.label: Denver Health Sliding Fee Discount Program (DHSFDP) for emergency care
rules.quote: If you live outside of Denver County, you can always receive emergency medical care at Denver Health, even if you qualify for Medicaid or CHP+

notes: Policy defines 'community' as Denver City/County residents; specialty care for non-residents is limited.
Current non-Denver patients who are uninsured and receiving an elective procedure or specialty service will continue to be seen through their course of that specific treatment.
Hospitals must screen all uninsured patients and insured patients who request screening for Health First Colorado, CHP+, Medicare, Emergency Medicaid, and financial assistance.
Hospitals must give patients the chance to apply for discounted care when they have services at the hospital.
A Denver County residency requirement is not needed to apply for Hospital Discounted Care (HDC).
Customers enrolled in a discount program (DHSFDP and HDC) must be screened every year by an enrollment specialist.
Falsifying information on family size, income, housing status (homelessness) or home location is considered fraud and must be reported to the state of Colorado.
DHSFDP and HDC are discount programs and not considered health insurance.
Health First Colorado (Medicaid) applications accepted anytime throughout the year; CHP+ and Connect for Health Colorado have open enrollment periods.
Service exclusions (cosmetic, transplant, research) not specified in this text.
Application deadlines, extraordinary collection action timing, first statement timing, and payment plan terms not specified in this text.

rule_dhsfdp_emergency may leave out a condition: Non-residents get emergency care, but DHSFDP does not apply to emergency care per policy.

disagreements_before: A household of 2 earning $68,000 a year (314.2% of the poverty line), living outside Colorado, uninsured, owing $10,000: the Nemotron 3 Ultra model gives help (amount not stated), the Nemotron 3 Super model gives no help.

A household of 3 earning $27,000 a year (98.8% of the poverty line), living outside Colorado, insured, and not under-insured as the policy defines it, owing $10,000, after non-emergency care: the Nemotron 3 Ultra model gives no help, the Nemotron 3 Super model gives help (amount not stated).
